builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Measuring Layer-wise Intrinsic Dimensionality of FFNs in LLMs via PCA
summary: Replaces the uniform FFN intermediate width convention (and uniform-width pruning) with per-layer widths allocated by PCA-measured intrinsic dimensionality, trained via knowledge distillation under a matched parameter budget. Costs a PCA calibration pass over a corpus, a distillation training run, and added architecture heterogeneity that complicates kernel and serving assumptions. Can fail when the teacher has low dimensionality dispersion (gains shrink to ~0.5 points), when the post-training distribution shifts activations away from the calibration profile, or when irregular per-layer widths negate inference efficiency on standard hardware.
rationale: Structured per-layer FFN width pruning is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU and the calibration cost is low, but the gain depends on the teacher's dimensionality dispersion and requires distillation, so workload-specific validation is warranted.

claims.statement: Replaces the uniform FFN intermediate width convention (and uniform-width pruning) with per-layer widths allocated by PCA-measured intrinsic dimensionality, trained via knowledge distillation under a matched parameter budget. Costs a PCA calibration pass over a corpus, a distillation training run, and added architecture heterogeneity that complicates kernel and serving assumptions. Can fail when the teacher has low dimensionality dispersion (gains shrink to ~0.5 points), when the post-training distribution shifts activations away from the calibration profile, or when irregular per-layer widths negate inference efficiency on standard hardware.

PCA-guided non-uniform FFN width allocation beats uniform-width pruning by +2.3 points on Qwen3-8B and +2.5 on Qwen2.5-3B under a matched parameter budget, with smaller gains (+0.9, +0.5) on lower-dispersion teachers; advantage persists through downstream SFT.
